transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I'm here because... well, my sleep is just messed up lately. I work overnight shifts, and when I get off, I just lie there. Wide awake. And then, if I do finally fall asleep... I wake up feeling scared. It just feels like I didn't get any rest at all.
When you wake up feeling scared, do you remember having a bad dream or nightmare before waking up?
No... I don't really remember any dreams. I just... I just wake up like that.
Have you ever experienced a brief period where you couldn't move or speak either when falling asleep or just after waking up?
No... I don't think so. I can move fine. I just... I haven't noticed anything like that.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt paralyzed or unable to move for a short time when you were falling asleep or just waking up?
No... like I just said, I haven't had that happen. I can move fine. I just... I don't get stuck like that or anything.
Have you ever seen, heard, or felt something that wasn't actually there either when you were falling asleep or just waking up?
No... I don't think so. I haven't seen anything weird like that. I just wake up scared, that's all.
Have you ever felt like you were briefly paralyzed or couldn't move your body when you were just waking up or falling asleep?
I... didn't you just ask me that? No. My body works fine when I wake up. I don't get paralyzed.
When you're trying to fall asleep or lying awake at night, do you find yourself thinking about the same things over and over again?
No, not really. I just... I just try to sleep. I don't really think about much.
When you're falling asleep or waking up, have you ever heard sounds or voices, or felt things that weren't really there?
I... you just asked me about that a minute ago. No. I don't hear anything like that.
Do you often wake up feeling as though you haven't slept at all, even if you were asleep for a long time?

Yeah. That's... kind of why I came in. My sleep is just all broken up now. I'll get off my overnight shift and just lie there wide awake. And when I do finally drift off, I just... I wake up scared. It feels like I never rested at all.
Have you ever felt your muscles go weak or give out suddenly, especially when you're feeling strong emotions like laughter, anger, or surprise?
No. I haven't had that happen.
Have you ever noticed your muscles suddenly feeling very weak or giving out when you're experiencing strong emotions like laughing, anger, or surprise?
You just asked me that, too. I already said no.
Do you find yourself falling asleep during the day, even when you're trying to stay awake, or have you ever fallen asleep unintentionally during normal activities?
No. Like I said, I can barely sleep when I'm actually trying to. So... no. I don't just fall asleep by accident.
Do you ever feel a sudden, strong urge to sleep during the day, even when you're trying to stay awake?
I just told you about sleeping during the day. No. I don't.
Have you ever found yourself suddenly entering a dream-like state or acting out dreams while still being in bed, like your mind is caught between dreaming and waking up?
No. I just lay there awake. I don't... I don't have dreams like that.
Would you say that your trouble sleeping only happens when you're working overnight shifts, or does it also happen when you're not working?

It happens... all the time. That's why I'm here. I get off my overnight shift and just... lie there. Wide awake. And even if I do drift off a little, I just wake up feeling scared. It doesn't feel like I rested at all.
Does your trouble falling and staying asleep only happen when you're on overnight shifts, or does it also occur when you're off work and trying to sleep at a regular night-time schedule?
Like I just said... it happens all the time. Even on my days off when I try to sleep at night. It doesn't make a difference.
Even though you have trouble sleeping at night, do you ever find yourself feeling excessively sleepy during the day or unintentionally dozing off at inappropriate times?
No. I don't... I don't really doze off. I'm just tired. But I don't fall asleep.
Do you often feel anxious or worried around the time you're trying to fall asleep or after waking up?
I don't really... I don't know about worried. I'm not lying there worrying about things, if that's what you mean. I just wake up feeling scared, like I told you. I don't know why.
Have you had trouble sleeping even before you started working overnight shifts, or did your sleep problems start only after beginning your night shift work?

No... it started after. It's been going on for... I guess about a year and two months. That's when my agency changed me to rotating overnight shifts... and gave me extra paperwork. So, yeah. It started then.
